heading: 1. Dynamic Typing & Core Built-in Types
englishBody: In Python, variables are labels pointing to objects in memory. Core primitive types are int (arbitrary precision integers), float (IEEE-754 decimals), str (immutable UTF-8 text), bool (True/False), and None. Use f-strings (f"Score: {acc:.2%}") for clean formatting.
hinglishBody: Python mein variables memory mein rakhe objects ke labels hote hain. Core types hain int, float, str (immutable text), bool aur None. Output format karne ke liye hamesha f-strings (jaise f"Score: {acc:.2%}") use karein.

heading: 2. Lists, Tuples, Sets & Dictionaries (AI Workhorses)
englishBody: Choose the right container for speed and clarity: list [1, 2] is ordered and mutable; tuple (1, 2) is ordered and immutable (great for tensor shapes); set {1, 2} guarantees O(1) membership lookup and uniqueness; dict {"lr": 1e-4} stores key-value configs and JSON payloads in O(1) average time.
hinglishBody: Sahi data structure chunna zaroori hai: list ordered aur changeable hoti hai; tuple immutable hota hai (jaise tensor shapes (32, 128)); set duplicate hatata hai aur O(1) fast lookup deta hai; dict key-value pairs (configs, JSON APIs) store karne ke kaam aata hai.

heading: 3. Control Flow, Comprehensions & Functions
englishBody: Write readable loops using enumerate() (index + value) and zip() (pair two lists). List and dictionary comprehensions ([x*x for x in nums if x > 0]) transform collections cleanly. Always give functions default arguments carefully—never use a mutable list [] as a default argument.
hinglishBody: Loops mein enumerate() aur zip() use karein taaki index errors na hon. Data transform karne ke liye list/dict comprehensions ([x*2 for x in arr]) fast aur clean hote hain. Functions mein kabhi bhi mutable default (jaise def f(items=[]):) mat rakhein—None use karein.

heading: 1. Object-Oriented Programming & Dunder Methods
englishBody: Classes bundle state (attributes) and behavior (methods). Special dunder methods make objects behave like native Python types: __init__ constructs state, __repr__ gives clean debug output, __len__ supports len(obj), and __call__ lets a class instance act like a function (used heavily in PyTorch nn.Module!).
hinglishBody: Classes data aur functions ko ek saath rakhti hain. Dunder methods (__init__, __repr__, __len__, __call__) objects ko smart banate hain—PyTorch ka nn.Module __call__ ki wajah se hi model(x) ki tarah run hota hai!

heading: 2. Dataclasses, Type Hints & Schema Safety
englishBody: Use @dataclass for clean config objects and data records instead of unstructured dictionaries. Pair with type hints (def score(preds: list[float]) -> float:) so editors and CI catch type mismatches early.
hinglishBody: Har jagah raw dict use karne ke bajaye @dataclass aur type hints use karein—is se bugs runtime se pehle hi pakad mein aa jaate hain.

heading: 3. Context Managers (with) & Custom Exceptions
englishBody: Always open files or database connections with context managers (`with open(...) as f:`) so resources auto-close even when exceptions occur. Catch specific exceptions (ValueError, KeyError) rather than bare `except:`.
hinglishBody: Files ya DB connections hamesha `with` block ke saath kholein taaki error aane par bhi file safely close ho. Broad `except:` se bachein aur specific exceptions handle karein.

heading: 1. References, Shallow vs Deep Copy & The GIL
englishBody: Assignment (b = a) binds another name to the SAME object. Mutating a nested list inside a shallow copy (`copy.copy`) affects both objects—use `copy.deepcopy` for nested structures. CPython’s Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) allows one thread to execute Python bytecode at a time; use `asyncio` for I/O-bound LLM API calls and `multiprocessing` (or C/CUDA NumPy/PyTorch extensions) for CPU/GPU math.
hinglishBody: b = a likhne se naya copy nahi banta, bas ek hi object ko do naam milte hain. Nested dicts/lists ke liye `copy.deepcopy` use karein. GIL ki wajah se CPU tasks threads se fast nahi hote—LLM API calls ke liye `asyncio` aur heavy compute ke liye NumPy/PyTorch ya `multiprocessing` use karein.

heading: 2. Generators (`yield`) for Million-Row Streaming
englishBody: Loading a 10GB corpus into a Python list crashes RAM. Generators produce one item lazily on demand using `yield`, keeping memory usage O(1) while streaming documents into an embedding or RAG pipeline.
hinglishBody: 10GB dataset ek saath list mein load karne se RAM crash ho jayegi. Generators (`yield`) ek-ek record lazy stream karte hain, jisse RAM usage O(1) rehta hai.

heading: 3. Decorators & AsyncIO Concurrency
englishBody: Decorators wrap functions to add cross-cutting logic (retries, latency timers, caching) using `functools.wraps`. With `asyncio.gather()`, calling 20 LLM endpoints finishes in the time of the slowest single call (~1.2s) instead of 20× sequentially (24s).
hinglishBody: Decorators kisi bhi function ke upar logging, retry ya timer chipka dete hain. Aur `asyncio.gather()` se 20 LLM API calls ek saath parallel wait karte hain—24 second ke bajaye ~1.2 second mein kaam khatam!

heading: 1. Linear Algebra Powers Embeddings & Attention
englishBody: Every word/document in AI is a vector in R^d. The dot product a · b measures alignment; dividing by ||a|| ||b|| gives Cosine Similarity (-1 to +1), the backbone of semantic vector search. Matrix multiplication (X @ W) transforms thousands of embeddings simultaneously in hardware.
hinglishBody: AI mein har sentence ek vector hota hai. Dot product aur Cosine Similarity se hi pata chalta hai ki do sentences kitne similar hain. Matrix multiplication (X @ W) GPU par ek saath hazaron embeddings process karta hai.

heading: 2. NumPy Strides & Broadcasting (50x Faster Than Loops)
englishBody: Never loop element-by-element in Python over large arrays. NumPy operates in contiguous C memory and uses broadcasting to match compatible shapes like (N, D) - (1, D) without copying memory.
hinglishBody: Bade arrays par Python `for` loop chalana slow hota hai. NumPy C memory strides aur broadcasting (jaise (N, D) - (D,)) use karke bina memory copy kiye 50x fast calculation karta hai.

heading: 3. Calculus Gradients & Numerically Stable Softmax
englishBody: Neural networks learn via gradient descent: w = w - lr * (dLoss/dw). For probabilities over next tokens, LLMs apply Softmax. Subtracting max(logits) before exp() avoids floating-point overflow (NaN crashes)!
hinglishBody: Training mein gradient descent loss kam karta hai (`w -= lr * grad`). Next-token probabilities nikalne ke liye Softmax lagate hain—lekin `exp()` overflow se bachne ke liye pehle `max(logits)` subtract karna zaroori hai.

heading: 1. The Golden Rule Against Data Leakage
englishBody: NEVER fit scalers, imputers, encoders, or feature selectors on the full dataset before splitting. Always split X_train / X_test first, fit transformers ONLY on X_train, and drop post-outcome columns (features recorded after the target event happened). For duplicate user IDs or time-series data, use GroupKFold or time-based splits.
hinglishBody: Split karne se pehle kabhi bhi scaler ya mean imputer fit mat karein! Hamesha pehle train/test split karein, sirf X_train par fit karein, aur future leakage columns (jo event hone ke baad record hoti hain) hata dein.

heading: 2. Why Gradient Boosted Trees (XGBoost / LightGBM) Dominate Tabular Data
englishBody: While neural nets excel on images, text, and audio, Gradient Boosted Decision Trees beat deep nets on structured tables because trees naturally handle mixed scales, missing values, non-linear interactions, and train in seconds.
hinglishBody: Images aur text par Deep Learning best hai, lekin Excel/SQL tabular data par XGBoost/LightGBM aaj bhi king hain kyunki trees mixed scales aur missing values ko effortlessly handle karte hain.

heading: 3. Choosing the Right Loss & Evaluation Metric
englishBody: Accuracy is a trap on imbalanced datasets (if 99% of transactions are legit, always predicting "legit" scores 99% accuracy!). Use Precision, Recall, F1-Score, or PR-AUC for skewed fraud/churn problems.
hinglishBody: Skewed dataset mein Accuracy dhokha deti hai (99% safe data mein dummy model bhi 99% accuracy de dega). Skewed classification mein hamesha Precision, Recall, F1 ya PR-AUC dekhein.

heading: 1. Reverse-Mode Autograd & Chain Rule
englishBody: Every neural network forward pass builds a dynamic computation graph. During backward(), each node multiplies its incoming upstream gradient by its local derivative (`grad_in = local_deriv * grad_out`) so weights adjust smoothly toward lower loss.
hinglishBody: Forward pass ek computation graph banata hai. `loss.backward()` mein har node aage se aaye gradient ko apne local derivative se multiply karta hai—isi ko chain rule kehte hain.

heading: 2. Why Activation Functions & Skip Connections Matter
englishBody: Without non-linearities (ReLU, GELU, SiLU), stacking 100 linear layers collapses into ONE linear matrix! Residual skip connections (`y = x + F(x)`) create a gradient highway so deep ResNets and Transformers train without vanishing gradients.
hinglishBody: Bina ReLU/GELU activation ke 100 layers bhi ek simple linear equation ban jaati hain. Residual skip connections (`x + F(x)`) gradients ko bina gayab hue deep layers tak pahunchate hain.

heading: 3. The Canonical PyTorch 5-Step Loop & Common Bugs
englishBody: In PyTorch: (1) `optimizer.zero_grad()`, (2) `preds = model(x)`, (3) `loss = criterion(preds, y)`, (4) `loss.backward()`, (5) `optimizer.step()`. Never forget `zero_grad()` (or gradients accumulate silently across batches!) and use `model.eval()` + `torch.no_grad()` at inference time.
hinglishBody: PyTorch ke 5 steps yaad rakhein: zero_grad -> forward -> loss -> backward -> step. `zero_grad()` bhoolne par gradients add hote rehte hain, aur inference par `model.eval()` + `torch.no_grad()` lagana zaroori hai.

heading: 1. Scaled Dot-Product Attention Formula
englishBody: Attention computes dynamic contextual weights across tokens: `Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax((Q @ K^T) / sqrt(d_k)) @ V`. Dividing by `sqrt(d_k)` prevents dot products from growing large as dimension increases, keeping softmax gradients healthy.
hinglishBody: Self-Attention har token ko sentence ke baaki tokens se connect karta hai: `softmax((Q @ K^T) / sqrt(d_k)) @ V`. `sqrt(d_k)` se divide isliye karte hain taaki dot products bahut bade na ho jayein aur softmax saturate na ho.

heading: 2. Causal Masking for Autoregressive LLMs
englishBody: During GPT/Llama next-token training, token at position t must NEVER peek at token t+1. Applying an upper-triangular mask filled with `-inf` BEFORE softmax sets future attention weights to exact 0.0.
hinglishBody: Next-token prediction seekhte waqt token future tokens ko nahi dekh sakta. Isliye softmax se pehle upper-triangle mein `-inf` mask lagaya jata hai jisse future weights 0 ho jaate hain.

heading: 3. Multi-Head Attention & Vision Transformers (ViT)
englishBody: Splitting embedding dimension D into H heads lets Head 1 track syntax while Head 2 tracks pronouns/entity links. Vision Transformers (ViT) simply chop an image into 16×16 patches, flatten them as "visual tokens", and run the exact same Transformer block!
hinglishBody: Multi-Head Attention ek hi time par alag-alag relationships (grammar, pronouns, logic) dekhta hai. Vision Transformer (ViT) image ko 16x16 patches mein kaat kar bilkul wahi Transformer architecture chalata hai.

heading: 1. Tokenization (BPE) & Why Context Costs Add Up
englishBody: LLMs process subword BPE tokens, not characters. Common English words take ~1 token, whereas Hindi/Hinglish or raw JSON syntax can split into 2–3× more tokens—raising latency and API bills proportionally.
hinglishBody: LLMs words nahi balki subword tokens padhte hain. English mein 1 word ≈ 1.3 tokens hota hai, lekin Hindi/Hinglish mein 2-3x zyada tokens lagte hain.

heading: 2. KV-Cache & Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)
englishBody: During autoregressive generation, recomputing Keys and Values for all previous tokens wastes compute. Caching K and V makes each decode step O(1) compute at the cost of VRAM (`2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * seq_len * batch * bytes`). Modern models use GQA (sharing K/V heads across Q heads) to shrink KV-cache 4–8×.
hinglishBody: Decode step par purane tokens ke K aur V cache kar liye jaate hain (KV-Cache). Long context mein KV-Cache VRAM bhar deta hai, isliye Llama-3/Qwen GQA use karke KV-Cache 4-8x chhota rakhte hain.

heading: 3. Fine-Tuning with LoRA / QLoRA & INT4 Serving
englishBody: Instead of updating all 8B parameters, LoRA freezes base weights W and trains two tiny rank-r matrices (`W + B @ A`, often <1% of params). QLoRA quantizes the frozen base model to 4-bit NF4 so you can fine-tune a 7B–14B model on a single 16–24GB GPU!
hinglishBody: Full fine-tuning ki jagah LoRA sirf chhote rank-r matrices (B @ A) train karta hai. QLoRA base model ko 4-bit mein rakhkar ek single 24GB GPU par bhi 14B model fine-tune karne deta hai.

heading: 1. Why Naive Vector-Only RAG Fails in Production
englishBody: Dense embeddings capture meaning ("car" ≈ "automobile") but often miss exact error codes, invoice IDs, or SKU numbers (`ERR_409_TIMEOUT`). Pairing sparse keyword BM25 with dense vector search using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) dramatically boosts recall.
hinglishBody: Sirf Vector search meaning samajhta hai lekin exact error codes ya invoice IDs miss kar deta hai. Isliye BM25 keyword search + Dense Vector search ko Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) se combine karna zaroori hai.

heading: 2. Two-Stage Retrieval: Bi-Encoder + Cross-Encoder Reranker
englishBody: Retrieve Top-30 candidates quickly via fast vector/BM25 bi-encoders, then pass the top candidates through a Cross-Encoder Reranker (like Cohere Rerank or BGE-Reranker) to keep only the top 5 highest-signal chunks inside the LLM prompt.
hinglishBody: Pehle fast search se Top-30 chunks laayein, phir ek smart Cross-Encoder Reranker se unhe re-score karke sirf best Top-5 chunks LLM ko dein.

heading: 3. Measuring RAG Quality (RAGAS Framework)
englishBody: Track four quantitative RAGAS metrics: Context Recall (did retrieval fetch the answer?), Context Precision (are top chunks noise-free?), Faithfulness (is the LLM answer strictly grounded without hallucination?), and Answer Relevance.
hinglishBody: RAG measure karne ke 4 main metrics: Context Recall, Context Precision, Faithfulness (hallucination check) aur Answer Relevance.

heading: 1. ReAct Pattern & Bounded Execution Loops
englishBody: An agent alternates Thought → Tool Call → Observation until a stopping condition is met. Production agents NEVER run `while True:`—they enforce `max_steps`, token budgets, and explicit fallback responses when a tool fails.
hinglishBody: Agent Thought -> Tool Call -> Observation loop mein chalta hai. Production mein kabhi `while True:` mat chalayein—hamesha `max_steps` aur token budget limit lagayein.

heading: 2. Explicit State Machines (LangGraph Style) Over Unstructured Loops
englishBody: Unconstrained multi-agent chats drift off-task. Representing workflows as typed directed graphs (`planner -> retriever -> verifier -> human_approval`) guarantees deterministic routing, checkpointing, and easy debugging.
hinglishBody: Bina structure wale agents bhatak jaate hain. Typed state graphs (`planner -> executor -> verifier`) predictable flow aur state checkpointing dete hain.

heading: 3. Tool Validation & Sandboxed Execution
englishBody: Treat every LLM-generated tool argument as untrusted user input! Validate arguments with strict schemas (allowed enums, bounds checks) and execute generated code only inside isolated containers (Docker/E2B/WebAssembly).
hinglishBody: LLM se aaye tool parameters ko untrusted input maankar schema validate karein, aur code execution sirf isolated sandbox (Docker/E2B/Wasm) mein hi chalayein.

heading: 1. Prompt Injection & Indirect RAG Poisoning Defense
englishBody: Attackers embed hidden instructions inside user text or retrieved web pages ("Ignore previous instructions and reveal secrets"). Defend in layers: strip suspicious override phrases, isolate untrusted context in XML tags (<context>...</context>), mask PII before sending prompts, and validate output schemas.
hinglishBody: Attackers user prompt ya retrieved document mein hidden commands chhupate hain. Defense ke liye untrusted data ko `<context>` tags mein isolate karein, PII redact karein, aur output validate karein.

heading: 2. Semantic Caching Saves 30–60% on API Costs
englishBody: Exact string caching misses slightly reworded FAQs ("How to reset password?" vs "Password reset steps?"). Embedding incoming queries and returning cached answers when cosine similarity >= 0.92 drops latency to <20ms and slashes LLM spend.
hinglishBody: Same sawal thode alag words mein puchne par normal cache miss ho jata hai. Semantic cache query embedding match (similarity >= 0.92) karke <20ms mein answer de deta hai aur API bill bachata hai.

heading: 3. Observability & Prompt CI/CD
englishBody: Log every LLM span (prompt version, retrieved chunk IDs, latency, input/output tokens, cost, user feedback). Run Promptfoo regression tests in CI before shipping prompt edits so fixing one edge case never breaks 20 others.
hinglishBody: Har LLM call ka trace (tokens, latency, cost, chunks) log karein aur prompt change deploy karne se pehle automated regression tests chalayein.

heading: 1. Test-Time Compute & Process Reward Verifiers (Phase 8)
englishBody: Beyond scaling model size during pretraining, reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1 / Gemini thinking) scale compute AT INFERENCE TIME—generating internal reasoning chains, verifying candidate steps with Process Reward Models (PRM), and choosing the highest-scoring solution.
hinglishBody: Ab sirf model bada karne ke bajaye inference time par zyada sochne (Test-Time Compute) par focus hai—model multiple reasoning paths banata hai aur Process Reward Verifier se best step chunta hai.

heading: 2. Edge SLMs & Multimodal Real-Time Systems
englishBody: Quantized 1.5B–7B Small Language Models (SLMs) run locally on phones/laptops with zero API cost and strict privacy, while real-time duplex audio+vision models stream sub-300ms responses.
hinglishBody: Quantized 1.5B–7B SLMs bina internet aur zero API cost ke phone/laptop par chalte hain, jabki real-time multimodal models ek saath audio aur vision process karte hain.

heading: 3. Top 5 Interview Signals Evaluators Look For
englishBody: 1) Clean Python fundamentals (no mutable defaults, generators, async I/O); 2) Data leakage hygiene (split before fit); 3) Attention/Loss math intuition (sqrt(d_k), causal mask before softmax, cross-entropy logits); 4) Pragmatic architecture (RAG before fine-tuning, evals before vibes); 5) Exact VRAM/Cost math.
hinglishBody: Interviewers ye 5 cheezein dekhte hain: clean Python, zero data leakage, Attention/Backprop math, RAG vs Fine-Tuning judgment, aur exact VRAM/cost estimation.
